cite: Commonwealth Mortgage Co. v. De Waltoff, 119 N.Y.S. 781
court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, First Department
holding_summary: Foreclosure purchaser becomes landlord by operation of law without attornment; summary proceedings for an apartment tenant's nonpayment of rent sustained.
notes: Mortgage foreclosure/attornment dispute over an apartment lease; does not bear on short-term letting practice.

court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, First Department
holding_summary: Innkeeper's liability for a guest's baggage continues for a reasonable time after the guest checks out and leaves, until baggage is actually removed.
notes: Hotel baggage/bailment liability case; does not address legal character or regulation of letting rooms.

court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, First Department
holding_summary: Covenant to pay rent did not survive statutory dispossession of the tenant absent express language making it survive.
notes: Ordinary commercial lease deposit/dispossession dispute; no bearing on short-term dwelling letting.

cite: Broadway Building Co. v. Fergusson, 116 N.Y.S. 630
holding_summary: Temporary office-suite occupancy pending reassignment created only a month-to-month tenancy, terminable on reasonable notice.
notes: Commercial office suite dispute, not residential lodging.

court: County Court of New York, Orleans County
holding_summary: A farm-on-shares working agreement did not create a master-servant relationship, so summary removal under the servant-removal statute was unavailable.
notes: Agricultural sharecropping/master-servant dispute; unrelated to lodging or short-term letting.

cite: Silver Lake Assembly v. Hard, 116 N.Y.S. 1061
court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, Fourth Department
holding_summary: Camp-meeting association's lien for annual lot taxes survived conveyance of tent/cottage lots because the lien provision was carried into the purchaser's own deed.
notes: Passing mention of tent/cottage lots occupied seasonally and of 'transient guests'; case is actually about deed covenants and tax liens on fee ownership of camp lots, not compensated short-term occupancy.

cite: Wilkes-Barre Realty Co. v. Levy, 114 N.Y.S. 713
holding_summary: An apartment tenant was not constructively evicted by noise and odors from a ground-floor occupant's table-boarding arrangement, because the landlord neither caused, authorized, nor knew of the disturbance; constructive eviction requires conduct committed, encouraged, or connived at by the landlord.

quotes.text: the agent of the plaintiff gave to a Mrs. Hunter, who occupied the ground floor of the building at the time the defendant made the lease, permission to keep “table boarders”; that the rooms were not leased as a boarding house, but as a private apartment, with the privilege of taking in such boarders.

the agent of the plaintiff gave to a Mrs. Hunter, who occupied the ground floor of the building at the time the defendant made the lease, permission to keep “table boarders”; that the rooms were not leased as a boarding house, but as a private apartment, with the privilege of taking in such boarders.
an eviction cannot be predicated of acts or conduct, however wrongful or distressing, unless committed, encouraged, or connived at by the landlord.

notes: Landlord expressly permitted a residential occupant to keep 'table boarders' in her private apartment (not a boarding house) as an ordinary incident of the lease, uncontested as unlawful; core holding is about constructive eviction, so relevance/polarity attach to the underlying factual premise rather than a squarely litigated point. Duration left unclear on the facts given (meal-boarding, not lodging nights).

cite: Doyle v. John E. Olson Realty Co., 116 N.Y.S. 834
court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, First Department
holding_summary: Court declined to answer, on an incomplete submission of controversy, whether restrictive covenants barring a theater/hotel/barroom use remained enforceable given neighborhood change.
notes: Restrictive covenant/zoning dispute over a proposed theater-hotel; mentions 'hotel' only as a prohibited use category, not letting practice.

court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, Fourth Department
holding_summary: Growing rye sown by a tenant under an oral crop-sharing agreement remained personalty reserved from a subsequent conveyance of the farm; grantee who agreed to honor the reservation was liable over to the grantor.
notes: Farm tenancy crop-ownership dispute; no bearing on short-term dwelling letting.

court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, Second Department
holding_summary: Where a servant occupied premises rent-free as part compensation for services, no conventional landlord-tenant relation arose, and the master could remove her with necessary force upon lawful termination of employment.
notes: Rent-free servant occupancy tied to employment, not compensated letting for pay by a householder.

holding_summary: Time was of the essence in a building contract; owner's payment of the contract balance and taking possession before completion did not waive a claim for delay damages measured by lost rents.
notes: Building-contract delay/damages dispute; loss-of-rent is just the damages measure, not a letting-practice question.

holding_summary: Under the 1905 hotel-keeper's lien statute, notice to the hotel of a third party's ownership given after property was brought onto the premises does not defeat the lien for charges already accrued.
notes: Hotel keeper's lien/notice dispute over a guest's piano; guest's ~2.5-month residency at the hotel is undisputed background, not litigated, so it doesn't bear on the character or regulation of letting.

court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, Third Department
holding_summary: State retained title to gospel-and-school and literature lots never sold by town vote; squatter-defendants without title could not defeat the state's ejectment claim by pointing to a defect in that title.
notes: Ejectment/public lands title dispute; unrelated to dwelling letting.

court: Supreme Court, Special Term, New York County
holding_summary: A dressmaking establishment run on restricted residential lots violated a covenant against 'business,' though the covenant did not reach the practice of a profession such as medicine.
notes: Restrictive covenant / business-vs-profession dispute; no lodging or boarding issue.

court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, First Department
holding_summary: Civil Rights Law's exclusive statutory penalty for denial of equal accommodations at a theater precluded an injunction remedy for a drama critic barred from defendants' theaters.
notes: Civil rights/public accommodation theater-admission case; statutory definition of 'place of public accommodation' quotes inn/hotel language only in passing.

court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, First Department
holding_summary: Lessee of a loft building was not liable for a subtenant employee's negligent handling of a hoistway that injured a plumber, where the lessee had no duty to supervise tenants' use of the hoistway during business hours.
notes: Commercial loft building negligence/premises-liability case; unrelated to residential letting.

court: Supreme Court, Trial Term, Wyoming County
holding_summary: A co-tenant in possession of the family homestead could not be charged rent but was liable for taxes and ordinary repairs; a void tax assessment could not be charged to co-tenants.
notes: Tenancy-in-common accounting among heirs occupying family homestead; not a compensated letting arrangement.

cite: Webber v. Franklin Brewing Co., 108 N.Y.S. 251
court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, First Department
holding_summary: Bar fixtures and similar saloon equipment installed by a commercial tenant were removable trade fixtures, not improvements surrendered to the landlord under the lease.
notes: Trade-fixture dispute over saloon equipment; commercial lease, not lodging.
